newsitem.title: INDIA: India sees economy growing at over seven percent.
newsitem.headline: India sees economy growing at over seven percent.

text.p: India said on Saturday it was confident its economy would grow at a real rate of seven percent or more, and inflation would stay in the 6.5-7.0 percent range in the fiscal year starting on April 1.

"Our view is that we will see real GDP growth of seven percent-plus and we will see perhaps inflation at most for the average of the year at 6.5 to 7.0 percent," Shankar Acharya, chief economic adviser in the Finance Ministry, told a news conference.
India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index (WPI) rose to 7.99 percent in the week ending February 8 from 7.73 percent in the previous week.
The government estimates that GDP will expand by 6.8 percent in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31, compared with 7.1 percent in the previous year.

Acharya said he thought WPI might go up by one or two percentage points in the remainder of the current fiscal year. "But I am quite confident that with this budget you will see a decline in the rate of inflation throughout next year."

He was speaking a day after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram unveiled a bold, business-friendly budget for the 1997/98 year that slashed taxes and tariffs and took the six-year-old reform of the Indian economy forward in a big leap.
"India has reached a place where achieving seven percent growth was possible," Chidambaram told parliament last month.

President Shankar Dayal Sharma also told parliament at the start of its budget session on February 20 that the government's aim of achieving annual growth in GDP of at least seven percent over the next five years was feasible.
